item.title: ProteinGuide (UC Berkeley / Listgarten lab, Nature Biotechnology 2026-07-29) — inference-time property guidance for ESM3, ProteinMPNN, MultiFlow without retraining; single round exceeds 7 rounds of directed evolution on adenine base editor; 75% success on multi-property Pareto design. Raygun (Duke / Singh lab, Nature 2026-07-29) — protein language model embeddings as fixed-dimensional probability distributions enabling miniaturization (10–50%), expansion, and sequence diversification; validated on fluorescent proteins, TurboID, and EGF variants with higher EGFR affinity; applicable to VHH/nanobody and antibody fragment engineering.
item.description: Third edition for July 30th — two items, both published July 29, 2026. First, Xiong, Gaur, Lukarska, Nisonoff, Oltrogge, Savage, Listgarten (UC Berkeley / HHMI; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03207-z; Nature Biotechnology 2026-07-29): ProteinGuide — on-the-fly Bayesian property guidance for pre-trained protein sequence generative models without retraining. Statistical framework unifies masked language models (ESM3), any-order autoregressive models (ProteinMPNN), and discrete diffusion/flow-matching models (MultiFlow) under shared training objectives and sampling distributions when masking noise is used, allowing one guidance algorithm to transfer across all architectures. Guidance algorithms: Taylor-Approximate Guidance (fast) and Discrete-time Exact Guidance (exact). Wet-lab validation: adenine base editor engineering — single round of ProteinGuide from a 2,000-variant pooled library surpasses activity achieved by seven rounds of directed evolution; resulting variants at <80% sequence identity to wild type. In silico: consistently outperforms fine-tuning and post-hoc filtering across 8 proteins for stability-guided design; 75% success rate on multi-property Pareto design (lead binding improved while off-target zinc binding reduced). Relevance: inject prior-round CDR screening, affinity maturation, or stability assay data into ProteinMPNN or ESM3 at inference time; model-agnostic framework does not lock to a specific architecture. arXiv preprint: 2505.04823. Second, Devkota, Shonai, Mao, Ko, Wang, Soderling, Singh (Duke University; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10842-8; Nature 2026-07-29): Raygun — length-independent protein miniaturization, modification, and augmentation using protein language model embeddings as probability distributions in fixed dimensions. Core innovation: encode each protein as a probability distribution (not a sequence) in fixed-dimensional space using PLM per-residue embeddings, making proteins of any length directly commensurable; length changes and substitutions become unified moves in the same latent space. Two parameters: substitution rate and length-change rate. Validated in cells: miniaturized fluorescent proteins (2 variants < 96th percentile of FPbase by size); miniaturized TurboID biotin ligase; expanded EGF to generate EGFR-binding variants with higher affinity than wild type. Miniaturization range 10–25% (some >50%). Functional sites preserved; sequence diversity introduced. Antibody/nanobody applications: VHH miniaturization for gene therapy payloads, CDR loop length diversification respecting scaffold, compact bispecific fragment design. Code: github.com/rohitsinghlab/raygun.
